clue.text: Find me book in modest cover

indicators.note: 'in' places the first words inside the word that follows them
a cover wraps around what it protects, so the adjective's letters enclose the rest

blocks.note: coy means bashful or modest
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for a book of theirs tucked inside a plain, unassuming jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests a dust jacket, but it is the instruction to wrap; 'Find' is the definition as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To come by something is to obtain or get hold of it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Copper one degree in error - he does his best!

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
BSc, Bachelor of Science
out as in wrong, as in a calculation that is out

explanation.surface: A policeman with a degree gets it wrong, though he tried hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal. The Cubs' promise was 'to do my best', their motto 'Dyb dyb dyb'.
explanation.definitionFit: Junior Scouts pledge to do their best, so the young member of the movement is the one trying hard.

clue.text: There's nothing under this short garment, mother

blocks.note: a miniskirt
British informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother wearing a very short skirt with nothing underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic description: nothing falls below the least amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum is the lowest possible amount, so by definition no quantity lies below it.

clue.text: Metal ship

blocks.note: first meaning: a silvery alloy of tin, antimony and copper
second meaning: the British royal yacht

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like one thing, a ship of metal; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannia metal is a pewter-like alloy, and HMY Britannia was the Queen's royal yacht.

clue.text: First couple of planes caught by King Kong in New York?

indicators.note: something caught by another is held in its grip, so the first letters sit inside the giant's name
the first couple of a word means just its opening two letters

blocks.note: King Kong is the giant ape of the film
the opening two letters of the word

explanation.surface: The film scene where King Kong swats biplanes from the Empire State Building.
explanation.walkthrough: PL goes inside BIG APE. The question mark admits that King Kong is a big ape only by description.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Apple is the long-standing nickname for the American city, popularised by jazz musicians.

clue.text: Interested by pub profits, too

blocks.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
the bar is where drinks are served
gain means profit

explanation.surface: Someone keen on the takings of a pub as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Into the bargain means in addition or as well, an idiom matching the adverb too.

clue.text: A small part of journey with expedition

blocks.note: taken as written
a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: One leg of a trip taken during an expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' looks like a journey but means speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an adverb meaning quickly or swiftly, and expedition is promptness.

clue.text: Amended page with phrase, possibly

indicators.note: something amended has been changed, so the letters are rewritten in another order

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for page
taken as written

explanation.surface: A page revised with a new form of words, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps and possibly are adverbs expressing uncertainty, interchangeable synonyms.

clue.text: Oscar nomination for important dramatic role

definitions.text: Oscar nomination for important dramatic role

blocks.clueFragment: Oscar nomination for important dramatic role
blocks.note: surface reading: an Academy Award nomination for a big acting part
setter's reading: the name Oscar Wilde chose for a character in The Importance of Being Earnest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' is Wilde, 'nomination' is naming, and 'important' points to the play's title; Jack Worthing's assumed name is the punning answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Wilde's comedy Jack calls himself by this name in town, and Gwendolen loves him for it.

clue.text: Visionary projects found the French over the border?

blocks.note: to found metal is to cast it
les is French for 'the' (plural)
from France, the country over the Pyrenees border

explanation.surface: Grand schemes established by the French across the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find or 'establish', but is the metalworking verb; the border is the one the French would cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Castles in Spain, like castles in the air, are daydreams or impractical schemes that will never happen.

clue.text: Epicure takes exam in European city ahead of time

indicators.note: a city that takes something holds it within its own letters

blocks.note: Bonn, the former West German capital
a viva is an oral examination at university
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A gourmet sits an exam in a German city and finishes early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead of time' reads as 'early', but it places the city before the abbreviation for time. A viva is a British university oral exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A bon vivant is a person devoted to good food and drink, just like an epicure or gourmet.

clue.text: Religious leader whose staff worked wonders

definitions.text: Religious leader whose staff worked wonders

blocks.clueFragment: Religious leader whose staff worked wonders
blocks.note: surface reading: a cleric whose employees achieved great things
setter's reading: a staff is a rod, and this priest's rod budded and turned into a serpent in Exodus

explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' means employees on the surface but a walking rod in the Bible story; Moses' brother cast his rod down before Pharaoh.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Israelite high priest, brother of Moses, carried a miraculous rod in the Book of Exodus.

clue.text: Firm agreement

blocks.note: first meaning: solid and densely packed
second meaning: a formal pact or treaty

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests a business deal; 'Firm' is an adjective here, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for something dense and solid, and a noun for a contract or pact between parties.

clue.text: Race of early ship-builders

blocks.note: first meaning: a classic flat horse race for fillies run at Epsom in England
second meaning: the trees whose timber built wooden warships

explanation.surface: A tribe or people known for building the first boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' looks like a people; it is the horse race. The ship-builders are the trees whose wood made the hulls, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Oak timber was the classic material of sailing warships, and the Oaks is a famous English horse race.

clue.text: Demoralise a would-be peacemaker

blocks.note: first meaning: to rob of courage or nerve
second meaning, split in two: a man from the United Nations

explanation.surface: Undermining the confidence of a diplomat trying to broker peace.
explanation.definitionFit: To unman someone is to deprive them of courage, and a United Nations envoy tries to keep peace.

clue.text: Military activity - duty's to guard monarch

indicators.note: to guard something is to surround it protectively, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: excise is a duty levied on goods; the 's is 'is'
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A soldier's job is to protect the king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duty' means a soldier's obligation on the surface but a tax here, and the monarch is the abbreviation for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A military exercise is a training manoeuvre carried out by troops.

clue.text: Compare edges of iron coin found in a bit of China?

indicators.note: used as a verb, edges means borders, so the first abbreviation sits around everything after it

blocks.note: cp. is the abbreviation for compare
taken as written
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
the ecu, an old French coin

explanation.surface: Comparing the rims of an iron coin dug up in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is capitalised to suggest the country; it is crockery. 'Edges' looks like a noun but is a verb meaning borders.
explanation.definitionFit: Crockery is called china, and a drinking vessel for a hot beverage is one piece of it.

clue.text: Work done by Lewis, always offering key support

blocks.note: Main Street, Sinclair Lewis's 1920 novel, abbreviated as in an address
ay (aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A writer's dependable output is what keeps something going.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is the chief support of something, originally the stay holding a ship's mainmast.

clue.text: With oils, a man contrived to show this beauty

indicators.note: something contrived is artfully put together, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter using oils manages to depict a lovely woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nearly describes Leonardo at work, painting in oils.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's famous portrait of a smiling woman is the world's best-known painted beauty.

clue.text: Performing daily, in theory at any rate

blocks.note: an actor performing is on
a daily is a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone who performs every day, at least supposedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like an adverb but is a noun, a daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: On paper means in theory rather than in practice, the idiom for what ought to happen.

clue.text: Finish off cosmetic treatment in part of car

indicators.note: finish off here means take the end off, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a beauty treatment for the face

explanation.surface: Completing a beauty treatment while sitting in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: FACIAL loses its L.
explanation.definitionFit: The facia is the dashboard, the panel in front of the driver holding the instruments.

clue.text: Ultimately entering correct way of life

indicators.note: a word entering another goes inside it

blocks.note: to cure is to put right
ult. is the dictionary abbreviation for ultimate or ultimately

explanation.surface: In the end, getting into the right lifestyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' looks like an adverb for 'in the end', but it is used as its dictionary abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A culture is the shared customs and beliefs of a people, their whole manner of living.

clue.text: In space, circling over polar region

indicators.note: the letters wanted are in the words that follow, sitting inside them
in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A satellite orbiting in space above the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circling' wants to be the reversal indicator, but it supplies letters; 'over' does the turning.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice-cap is a permanent sheet of ice covering the land around the Poles.

clue.text: Bobby promises to pay in full

blocks.note: a bobby is a British policeman
IOUs are written promises of payment

explanation.surface: A policeman pledges to settle his debts completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pay in full' reads as one phrase; the definition is 'full' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Copious means plentiful or abundant, describing something full and generous in quantity.

clue.text: Authorises work - lady is ignoring the odds

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones in place

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A woman approves a job while beating the bookmaker's odds.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'work lady is' is the source, not just 'lady is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To okay something is to approve or sanction it, the informal synonym for authorise.

clue.text: Girl getting involved with men is a troublemaker

indicators.note: letters getting involved become tangled up together, so they are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl who gets mixed up with men is causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary mischievous sprite blamed for mechanical faults, so a troublemaker.

clue.text: Drink caught up with the old man

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Having a drink with your dad once you have woken up.
explanation.walkthrough: A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is a cup of tea, the everyday British hot drink.

clue.text: Opposing legal authority in battle

blocks.note: agin is dialect for against
a court of law

explanation.surface: Taking on the courts in a legal fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry V defeated the French at this 1415 engagement during the Hundred Years' War.

clue.text: Hum, being without skills in unaccompanied singing

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word lies around the other

blocks.note: hum and pong are both British slang for a bad smell
arts are skills or crafts

explanation.surface: Humming because you can't hold a tune in a choir singing without instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hum' looks musical but is British slang for a bad smell, and 'without' is used in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-song is a choral piece for several voices, traditionally sung without instrumental accompaniment.

clue.text: Steam yacht goes round ocean, returning in fleet

indicators.note: one thing going round another encircles it
returning means coming back the way it went, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: SY is the abbreviation for steam yacht
the deep is the sea

explanation.surface: A steamship sails around the ocean and returns with the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like a group of ships but is the adjective meaning fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means swift or nimble, so it equals quick or rapid.
